reviews.review:
I genuinely do not understand this game. Like it has charm, but it's just... Boring and a mess. I have played through 12 campaign missions so far, and they are all repetitive and monotonous, and they're not only repetitive from say, mission 2 and 3 being way too similar in gameplay, but like, within the missions themselves, it's repetitive. Like things drag on for WAYYY too long. Enemies are just bullet sponges, you shoot down a wave of enemies... Oh there's another wave of enemies now. Nothing really has changed. You just get more funny dialogue, and more of the exact same enemy to fight, when you were already wondering when this was all going to end because it just drags on. It's not challenging, it doesn't keep you occupied in any other sense than you just move and strafe around and hold down or click the mouse button. The dialogue is the only thing that truly makes it entertaining. 

It tries to be a looter-shooter in a sense, where you have to run around and pick up armor and weapon boxes. The problem is, this isn't fun. The controls are quite stiff, especially when sprinting as the ranger. The game is full of weird design decisions. Looting isn't fun in this game, yet it's such a big part of it. Gunplay is stale and repetitive, varying some from weapon to weapon. I'm baffled as to why some of the weapons are semi-auto with 30 round magazines that take multiple hits to kill enemies... When this is a literal horde shooter... Have they not heard of carpal tunnel? Basic user experience testing? I'm sure if I put in another 10 hours I'd be "oh... that's cool." And be mildly to moderately entertained by some weapon unlocks, but honestly... Time is important to me and I'm not going to accept a grind like that. 

This seems like a game that should have come out in 2009 (graphics AND gameplay) that we'd all remember fondly as having an important part of our childhoods, but not necessarily a game with the best replay value. 

2 hours in, and I have utterly lost interest. I think I've given more than enough time for the game to attempt to hook me. It's just... point, click, shoot, run, some other classes have more to them than that, but... I don't know, this game is just so... Lacking.

Like you start out and you find it novel and fun, somewhat nostalgic even. As I said, it represents games of the past. But not entirely in a good way. You can go back and play Sly Cooper and Ratchet and Clank and have a blast with the originals. This? This seems like something to occupy young children with very little substance beyond that. 

Maybe I just haven't gotten to "the good part," but every game designer and game studio should know that you do not let any player play for 2 hours without trying to engage that player and convince him to keep playing. This game has just failed at doing that for me.

tbh honest i don't wanna spoil anything but this game is amazing and worth every penny

i would buy it just for the dialogue alone, the gameplay (while equally amazing) is a huge bonus
